item.title: Re: Heed the Voct
item.content:encoded:
And other secretions. When I realized the potential to make them be the explanation for mysterious scrapes and bruises in the night, I loved it.

Plus, it's be one of the most common hypnagogic hallucinations. Nearly half of all adults who experience hypnagogia report the sensation and appearance of something sitting or standing on their chest, looking at them. Why not make it these guys?

Plus, I like the SIDs suggestion. As a parent, anything threatening to babies hits my "scare" button.

item.title: Heed the Voct
item.content:encoded:
Include what Voct said in the description. Just do it. Their desire to disassemble things would give them easy access through someone's door or windows "in the wild".

You wake up, you think you see a shadowy figure at the foot of your bed. In horror, you scramble to turn on the light and… there's nothing there. You roll over, disturbed, unharmed, but feeling drained and your bedroom door creaks only a whisper as -something- leaves your well-lit room.

Also, if their song caused the sleeper to generate more eye gunk than usual… that's even better!

EDIT:
This SCP has the potential to be one of the most horrifying on the site.
Downvote for adorable semi-invisible teddybear that sings to you in your sleep.
Upvote for terrifying night creature which you can't see that both causes and feeds on your eye secretions while you're asleep.

The picture is amazing, but the actual article is just kinda meh. It's a cool nonexistant animal, but it's really much too likeable to make a good SCP. To quote the general tips section of the how to write:

You should always aim to create something that scares the living daylights out of people, not something cool. If you think, "Huh, I'd like to have this SCP", you're doing it wrong. If the knowledge this object is in your house doesn't make you jump out the window into the garden a story below, you're probably doing it wrong.
